**"Don't think! Feeeeel."** — Bruce Lee, *Enter the Dragon*. That is the method
here, and it is meant literally.

Every module starts with something you do with your own hands, before anything
is defined. You trace the seven bridges of Königsberg on a map and fail, again,
to cross each one exactly once. You count how many of your own friends know
each other. You cut cables out of a power grid, one at a time, until the towns
go dark. The definition arrives afterwards, as a name for something you have
already felt.

No prior network science is assumed. The main text asks no linear algebra of
you; the derivations sit on each module's appendix page, to take or to leave.
Code is folded shut until you click it.

Outside class you hand in two things: a [Pair Notebook](course/pair-notebook.qmd)
— a module taught as a one-on-one session with an AI tutor in your terminal,
where the conversation is what gets graded, not the code — and a [Group
Mini-Project](course/mini-project.qmd) built with up to two teammates.
[Activities and grading](course/activities.md) lists everything that counts.

## The nine modules

One question opens the course, and each of the nine modules asks another. Every
question is a link into the lecture note; the worksheet under it is the one you
do before that lecture, with a pencil.

::: {.stop}
[Start]{.stop-no} [Why Networks?](intro/why-networks.qmd){.stop-title}

[Why do we need a science of networks instead of ordinary statistics?]{.stop-q}
:::

::: {.stop}
[M01]{.stop-no} [Euler Tour](m01-euler_tour/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[Can you walk a city crossing each bridge exactly once — and how would you ever prove you cannot?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [the Königsberg bridges](https://estebanmoro.org/pdf/netsci_for_kids/the_konisberg_bridges.pdf) (PDF, hosted by Esteban Moro)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M02]{.stop-no} [Small World](m02-small-world/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[Why is a stranger on the other side of the world only about six handshakes away?]{.stop-q}

Worksheets: [Six Handshakes](m02-small-world/pen-and-paper/six-handshakes.pdf) · [Turning the Dial](m02-small-world/pen-and-paper/turning-the-dial.pdf) · [Do Your Friends Know Each Other?](m02-small-world/pen-and-paper/do-your-friends-know-each-other.pdf)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M03]{.stop-no} [Robustness](m03-robustness/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[How much of a network can you destroy before it falls apart — and does it matter whether the damage is random or deliberate?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [Build it, Break it, and Build it Back](m03-robustness/pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M04]{.stop-no} [Friendship Paradox](m04-node-degree/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[Why do your friends have more friends than you do?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [Reading Heavy Tails](m04-node-degree/pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M05]{.stop-no} [Clustering](m05-clustering/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[What is a community in a network, and how would you know if the one you found is real?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [Discovering Friend Groups](m05-clustering/pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M06]{.stop-no} [Centrality](m06-centrality/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[Which node is the most important — and important in what sense?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [Who's the Big Cheese in the University Clubs?](m06-centrality/pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M07]{.stop-no} [Random Walks](m07-random-walks/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[What does a network look like to a walker who has no idea where they are going?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [Where Does the Drunkard Sleep?](m07-random-walks/pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M08]{.stop-no} [Embedding](m08-embedding/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[How do you turn a network into coordinates without throwing away what makes it a network?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [From Matrix to Map](m08-embedding/pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf)
:::

::: {.stop}
[M09]{.stop-no} [Graph Neural Networks](m09-graph-neural-networks/01-concepts.qmd){.stop-title}

[An image filter slides over every pixel in the same way. What do you slide over a network, where no two nodes have the same neighborhood?]{.stop-q}

Worksheet: [Convolution and the Weisfeiler-Lehman Test](m09-graph-neural-networks/pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf)
:::
